mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW M3 E90 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt S65B40 supplied and fitted typically runs £8,500-£12,000 through an independent specialist, against £13,000-£17,000 at a main dealer. Used engines start from around £3,000 supply-only, and reconditioned units with bearings addressed run £5,500-£7,500 supply-only. Fitting adds labour on top of any supply-only price.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of rod bearing wear in an S65 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most commonly reported early warning is a knocking or rattling noise from the bottom end, particularly on cold start-up, though many engines show no symptoms before wear is advanced. Watch for metallic particles in the oil and a drop in oil pressure at idle. If you hear knocking, stop driving and have the engine inspected before it's used again.

mainEntity.name: Should I replace the rod bearings before they fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - preventative replacement by 60,000-70,000 miles is standard UK specialist advice regardless of symptoms. Preventative replacement costs £1,200-£2,000, against an £8,500+ rebuild if wear reaches the crankshaft. Ask any specialist quote whether it uses upgraded, non-factory bearing shells.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an E90 M3?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most E90/E92/E93 M3s, currently worth roughly £13,000-£35,000 in the UK, yes - a rebuilt engine costs well within the car's value, especially against a rare naturally-aspirated V8 with no cheaper substitute. Average-condition cars are commonly valued around £25,000, comfortably above the £8,500-£12,000 rebuild cost.

mainEntity.name: Does the Coupe, Sedan or Convertible use a different engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: No - the E90 Sedan, E92 Coupe and E93 Convertible all share the identical S65B40 4.0-litre V8, with no differences in specification, output or known issues between body styles. The Convertible carries extra weight from its folding hardtop but this has no engine impact.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW M3 E90 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rod bearing replacement is typically a 1-2 day job. A full engine supply and fit generally takes longer once removal, fitting and running-in are accounted for - always confirm turnaround when comparing quotes.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW M3 E90 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The E90-generation M3 (2007-2013) was the only M3 ever built with a V8. Sold in the UK across three body styles on shared mechanicals, it's the enthusiast benchmark for naturally-aspirated M cars.

milestones.description: Launched with the S65B40 4.0L V8, derived from the S85 V10, producing 420hp at 8,300rpm.
UK sales begin across Sedan (E90), Coupe (E92) and Convertible (E93); Coupe becomes the best-seller at roughly two-thirds of the 8,262 UK M3s sold.
BMW revises the rod bearing spec (088/089 shells to updated 702/703 tin-aluminium design) in response to premature wear reports.
Competition Package (ZCP) arrives on Sedan and Coupe; the ultra-limited 444bhp M3 GTS lands, with only 7 reaching the UK.
Production ends; replaced by the F80, which switches to a twin-turbo inline-six - why this page covers the E90 generation only.

commonProblems.h3: Reliability on the E90-generation M3 comes down to one component: the S65B40's rod bearings - the issue that dominates replacement demand, and one where catching it early is far cheaper than waiting. Rebuilt S65 units through EnginesMarket use upgraded bearing shells, backed by a minimum 12-month warranty.

problems.h4: Rod Bearing Wear - Why the S65B40 V8 Needs Attention Before It Fails
problems.typicalFailureMileage: widely reported from 50,000 miles; preventative replacement recommended by 60,000-70,000 miles regardless of symptoms
problems.rootCause: factory rod bearing clearance was tighter than typical engineering practice recommends, restricting oil film thickness and accelerating wear under the S65's high-rpm operation.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Subframe and steering rack removed, worn bearings swapped for upgraded shells, engine mounts typically inspected/replaced at the same time
repairOptions.longevity: The right call for any E90 M3 approaching 60,000-70,000 miles with original bearings - a planned 1-2 day job

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt S65B40 with upgraded bearing shells, revised valvetrain, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Where bearing wear has already progressed to spun bearings or crankshaft damage - a preventative job is no longer possible

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical UK M3 E90/E92/E93 trades in the region of £13,000-£35,000, averaging around £25,000 `[THIRD-PARTY]`. That puts most cars in the £15,000+ band, where a full replacement is small relative to value - and the £1,200-£2,000 preventative fix is trivial by comparison. Only the highest-mileage, lowest-value cars warrant weighing a full rebuild bill carefully first.
problems.recommendation: Approaching 60,000 miles with original bearings? Book the preventative job now - £1,200-£2,000 against an £8,500+ rebuild if it's left too late. Already knocking or finding metal in the oil? Don't drive it further; a rebuilt engine with upgraded bearings is the only durable fix at that point.
